_doc: Spatial motifs and the tertiary-lymphoid-structure score. The triad *definition* comes from the literature (see triad.source); only the operational spatial parameters live here. The tetrad is an exploratory extension defined by this analysis, NOT by the triad paper.

triad.rule: A CD8 T cell is a triad anchor iff at least one CD4 T cell AND at least one dendritic cell lie within `radius_um` of its centroid.
triad.display_thinning_note: Greedy spatial thinning so drawn rings don't overlap; affects display only, not the anchor count.

source.citation: Espinosa-Carrasco G, et al. Intratumoral immune triads are required for immunotherapy-mediated elimination of solid tumors. Cancer Cell. 2024 Jul 8;42(7):1202-1216.e8.
source.what_to_extract: Which three cell types form a triad (CD8 T cell, CD4 T cell, antigen-presenting dendritic cell) and why their co-localization matters (CD4 licenses CD8 cytotoxicity / prevents exhaustion). The 20 um radius below is our spatial operationalization of 'co-localized' for Xenium centroids, not a number from the paper.

tetrad.rule: A triad anchor that additionally has at least one macrophage within `radius_um`.

source.note: Exploratory 4-cell niche defined in this workshop's parent analysis; it is NOT from the Espinosa-Carrasco paper. Present it as our extension, not as established literature.

tls_score._doc: Germinal-centre maturity score for a lymphoid aggregate, evaluated over a core radius around the aggregate centroid. Higher = more textbook mature TLS.
tls_score.marker_positive_rule: gene raw count > 0 in that cell
